answer: Copying the same citations across 200 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 200 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the horizon index resolves every citation against the bridge checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the glacier audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 2579 identities would post 2357 proofs and burn roughly 16 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
